title: Pay Per Call International: How to Run It Abroad
h1: Pay per call international: how to run campaigns outside one country
description: Pay per call international explained: number formats, buyer hours, billable-call rules and routing across countries. See how to set it up.
faq: Does pay per call work outside the US?
Yes. Any business that closes sales by phone can pay for qualified calls. The model is the same; number formats, time zones, billable-call definitions and local rules change by country.
How do I handle buyers in different time zones?
Set hours and daily caps per buyer in that buyer's own time zone, and use waterfall routing or bidding with a fall-back so calls skip closed buyers.
Do call recording rules differ between countries?
Yes. Rules on recording, consent and do-not-call differ by country, so check your obligations with your own counsel before running in each market.
body:
Pay per call international means running pay-per-call campaigns where callers, buyers or publishers sit outside a single country, and the model works the same way: a buyer pays for qualified phone calls, and a publisher or affiliate earns a payout for sending them. What changes abroad is not the idea but the details: number formats, call hours across time zones, what counts as a billable call, and which rules apply to recording and consent.

Why pay per call is no longer only a US model

Pay-per-call grew up around US insurance, legal and home services, but the logic travels. Any business that closes sales by phone, such as a clinic in Dubai, a solar installer in Sydney, a law firm in London or a loan broker in Mumbai, can pay for calls instead of clicks. If you already read our guide on what pay per call is, the international version adds a few extra decisions on top.

What changes when campaigns cross borders

Number formats and dialling

Every country formats numbers differently: trunk prefixes, area code lengths and mobile ranges vary widely. A call-routing system that assumes one format will mishandle blocked-number lists, repeat-caller checks and buyer destinations. Store numbers in a consistent international format and test every buyer destination before sending traffic.

Time zones and buyer hours

A buyer in Singapore and a buyer in Canada are never open at the same time. Hours and daily caps need to be set per buyer, in that buyer's own time zone, so that a call is never sent to a closed office. This is also the cheapest way to protect your publishers from calls that go unanswered and then get disputed.

Definitions of a billable call

Agree in writing what makes a call billable: a minimum duration, a connected status, a unique caller within a set window. Disputes are rarely about money; they are about two parties using different definitions. This matters more across borders, where you may never meet your counterpart.

Rules on recording, consent and do-not-call

Rules about call recording, consent, privacy and do-not-call lists differ by country, and sometimes by region within a country. This article is not legal advice. Check your obligations with your own counsel for every country you plan to run in, and decide whether a spoken recording notice is needed before a call is recorded.

Number types

Whether local, toll-free or other number types are practical depends on the country and on what is available when you set up, so do not assume the same number type will work everywhere. Plan your numbers per market and confirm availability before you promise anything to a buyer or publisher.

Targeting by country and state

The simplest way to keep international traffic clean is to target each campaign to the places a buyer actually serves. A buyer who only takes calls from one country or one state should never receive anything else. Keep one campaign per buyer region, give each its own rules, and you avoid mixed traffic that is impossible to price fairly.

Routing calls to the right international buyer

Two routing styles cover most needs:

  • Waterfall routing: try buyers in order of priority, skipping any that are closed, over their daily cap or blocked for that caller, and fall through to the next one.
  • Real-time bidding: ping buyers in parallel and send the call to the highest bid above your minimum. See how real-time call bidding works and our page on real-time call bidding software.

Whichever you pick, set a fall-back so a call is never dropped when nobody can take it.

Paying publishers fairly across markets

Payout rates rarely suit every country equally: a call in one market can be worth far more than in another. Set per-affiliate payout rates so you can reflect that, and give publishers a portal where they can see their own calls and downloadable statements. Our guide on pay per call affiliate payouts goes deeper, and affiliate payout software shows what to automate.

How to do it in Insight Dial

Insight Dial can be used by businesses in any country, and the pay-per-call features cover the points above. This is how a setup typically works:

  1. Create a campaign per buyer region and set country and state targeting.
  2. Add buyers with their hours, daily caps, blocked numbers and repeat-caller blocks, then choose waterfall routing or real-time bidding with a minimum bid and a fall-back.
  3. Turn on the pre-transfer check so a buyer is verified before a call is passed.
  4. Set per-affiliate payout rates and give publishers and buyers their own portals with downloadable statements.
  5. Use quality grades (Good, Watch, Poor) and auto-pause so sources sending too many short calls stop automatically.
  6. Run the guided setup checklist and the test-call tool before live traffic. Our pay per call launch checklist has the full list.

Pricing is pay as you go, a per-minute call rate plus a monthly price per tracking number from a topped-up balance. See pricing, and browse the pay-per-call industries hub for vertical examples such as insurance and legal.

A simple international starting plan

  • Pick one country and one vertical first.
  • Write down the billable-call definition and share it with every buyer and publisher.
  • Confirm your compliance position with your own counsel for that country.
  • Test calls end to end, then start with small caps and widen them as quality grades stay good.
